quick: 1 drop in affected eye once daily
Avoid in late pregnancy; use only if clearly needed
Not relevant for topical eye use
summary: Bromfenac 0.09% ophthalmic solution is a topical NSAID used to treat postoperative inflammation and reduce ocular pain after cataract surgery. One drop is instilled into the affected eye once daily starting 1 day before surgery and continued through 14 days postoperatively. Systemic absorption is negligible; key local risks include delayed healing and corneal effects.
indications: Treatment of postoperative inflammation in patients who have undergone cataract extraction
Reduction of ocular pain in patients who have undergone cataract surgery

dosage.n: Begin 1 day before surgery, continue on day of surgery and through first 14 days postoperatively

admin: Instill one drop into the affected eye once daily
Start dosing 1 day prior to cataract surgery and continue through the first 14 postoperative days
If using other topical ophthalmic drugs, separate each by at least 5 minutes
Avoid touching the dropper tip to the eye or any surface to prevent contamination
moa: Bromfenac is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug that blocks prostaglandin synthesis by inhibiting cyclooxygenase 1 and 2. Prostaglandins mediate intraocular inflammation, disrupting the blood-aqueous barrier and increasing vascular permeability; bromfenac reduces these effects.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to bromfenac or any component
relative: Known sulfite sensitivity (solution contains sodium sulfite)
Complicated ocular surgeries, corneal denervation or epithelial defects
Diabetes mellitus, ocular surface disease or repeat ocular surgery (higher corneal adverse event risk)
monitor: Patients with bleeding tendencies or on agents that prolong bleeding

preg: No adequate well-controlled studies in pregnant women (former Pregnancy Category C). Because of the known effects of prostaglandin-inhibiting drugs on the fetal cardiovascular system (premature closure of the ductus arteriosus), avoid use during late pregnancy. Use only if clearly needed.
lact: It is not known whether topical bromfenac is excreted in human milk; systemic exposure is negligible. Exercise caution when administered to a nursing woman.
renal: No dose adjustment needed; systemic concentration after ocular dosing is estimated to be below the limit of quantification.
hepatic: No dose adjustment needed; systemic absorption is negligible after ophthalmic administration.

moderate: Topical or systemic corticosteroids - additive risk of delayed healing and corneal complications
Other topical NSAIDs - increased risk of corneal adverse events
minor: Agents that prolong bleeding time (aspirin, anticoagulants) - theoretical increased ocular tissue bleeding
interactions.alcohol: Not relevant for topical eye use.
interactions.diagnostics: No clinically significant laboratory interference expected.

emergency: Sulfite-related anaphylactic or severe asthmatic reaction

monitoring: Corneal integrity and signs of keratitis during therapy
Symptoms of allergic reaction in sulfite-sensitive patients
counsel: Use exactly one drop in the operated eye once daily as directed
Do not touch the dropper tip to the eye or any surface
Remove contact lenses before instilling; do not wear lenses during therapy
Separate from other eye drops by at least 5 minutes
Report any eye pain, redness, vision changes or signs of infection promptly
pk: Plasma levels below quantification limit (50 ng/mL)
pearls: Once-daily dosing is a convenience advantage over older twice-daily ocular NSAIDs
Watch for corneal melting, especially in diabetics, dry eye, and repeat ocular surgery
Contains sodium sulfite - caution in sulfite-sensitive and asthmatic patients
Concomitant topical steroids may further delay healing
missed: If a dose is missed, instill it as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the once-daily schedule. Do not use extra drops to make up for a missed dose.
overdose: Topical ocular overdose is unlikely to cause systemic toxicity given negligible absorption. Accidental ingestion: drink fluids to dilute and treat symptomatically. Excessive instillation can be flushed from the eye with lukewarm water.
